model.architecture: Hybrid LFM2 text backbone (16 layers: gated short-convolutions + grouped-query attention, hidden 2048, 64k vocab) with the same large SigLIP2 vision tower as the 3B (27 layers, hidden 1152).

variants.quantization: text int4 blockwise-32 OCTAV linears, int8 embedding + lm_head; vision tower int8

recommended.reason: the Android path measured on a Pixel 8a (Tensor G3): 22.1 tok/s decode on gpu; the same phone's cpu row decodes 13.6 tok/s; the repo's LFM2.5-VL-1.6B_int8.litertlm decodes 15.9 tok/s on the same device and backend, so this file carries the class

measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 54.2 tok/s decode / 1062.9 prefill, peak 792 MB, init 3.1 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-25, 1 run) against CPU 42.69-50.85 decode / 95.7-127.3 prefill, peak 1330 MB, init 3.0 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken - a measured win for gpu on decode (1.2x) and prefill
card: iOS Metal fails at engine creation for this family, tracked upstream in [LiteRT-LM#3129](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM/issues/3129) — use CPU on iOS

platform_notes: Context (KV cache) 4096 max; one image per prompt, resized to 512x512 -> 256 tokens, PNG/JPEG via --attachment.
--vision-backend cpu|gpu selects the vision encoder backend independently of the text backend; text-only prompts work without --attachment.
The text graph delegates fully on Android OpenCL (543/543 nodes, zero rejected ops).
int4 prefills slower than int8 on CPU (blockwise-int4 repacking) but decodes markedly faster — pick by whether prompts or outputs dominate.
Galaxy S26 GPU gate covers engine creation and the text path only (no image in the gate prompt); the vision path on the GPU is not measured there. XNNPACK takes 1 of 4 nodes in main.
Text gate 8/8 on both variants on cpu & gpu: text is perfect across every configuration and backend.

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (6443 ops across 12 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: On litert-lm 0.16.0 and current main only the top quarter of the image reaches the model; captioning, colour questions and OCR of a large dominant subject work, but positional questions (locate, count, enumerate) come back wrong with no error.

Cause: a shrink-factor assumption in the runtime's vision path, reported upstream as LiteRT-LM#3246; affects every LFM2.5-VL bundle (2x2 pixel-unshuffle lives in the adapter, runtime assumes the encoder).
Band-ruler check (16 numbered bands): the 1.6B degenerates into a runaway count rather than cutting off cleanly; the repaired build returns 1..16.
A repaired build exists (pooling moved into the exported encoder) but the published files were not replaced pending the upstream fix; open a discussion if needed.
iOS Metal (GPU) fails at engine creation for this family (LiteRT-LM#3129); use CPU on iOS.

Image gate 3/5 on-device at every quantization level, including an unquantized probe build: shape and counting fixtures miss (they sit below the visible quarter — the runtime defect, not conversion loss).
